note: The fuzzer input is parsed as a uSWID header; the header supplies hdrsz and payloadsz for the embedded coSWID CBOR payload.
The input-controlled header size selects where the embedded payload starts.
The input-controlled payload size bounds the bytes copied from the uSWID container.

code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
note: With no compression, the selected CBOR bytes become the coSWID payload.

code: fw2 = fu_bytes_new_offset(payload, offset_tmp, payloadsz - offset_tmp, error);
note: The complete attacker-controlled CBOR payload is passed to a new coSWID firmware parser.
The CBOR map from the payload is decoded into libcbor items without normalizing integer widths.
A version-scheme tag in the root map routes the attacker-controlled unsigned integer to the version-scheme reader.
The validation only checks that the item is an unsigned integer, not that it was encoded with enough bytes for a 16-bit accessor.
A one-byte CBOR integer reaches cbor_get_uint16, which reads two bytes from storage allocated for the smaller integer encoding.
